artifacts.summary: Root-causes the silent staleness (no loader defect; regeneration is deliberately pull-only with no ambient signal, reproduced live on ~/.dotfiles) and recommends stamping a per-extension source-store git revision into .claude-extensions.json plus a cheap non-blocking WARN in command-gate-in.sh.

next_steps: Run /plan 18 to create an implementation plan for the source-git-head stamping (state.lua/init.lua) plus the command-gate-in.sh / check-deploy-freshness.sh preflight WARN.

memory_candidates.content: In this repo's Lua-driven extension loader (lua/neotex/plugins/ai/shared/extensions/{loader,init,state}.lua), manager.resync_all/manager.load never diff against installed_files or manifest version -- every load force-copies every declared file unconditionally (loader.copy_category has only three skip conditions: .syncprotect, symlink guard, and root_files install-once). A consuming repo's .claude/ tree only ever drifts stale because the deploy mechanism was never re-invoked after the source store changed -- regeneration is deliberately pull-only (context/patterns/regeneration-is-manual-only.md) with one narrow automated exception (skill-orchestrate's inter-cycle checkpoint). Do not assume a stale-deploy report implies a copy-engine bug without first checking whether a resync ran at all.

state.lua's mark_loaded already stamps an absolute source_dir path into every consuming repo's .claude-extensions.json per extension (identical machine-local path across repos). This is the ready-made building block for a cheap staleness check: pair it with a sibling source_git_head field (git log -1 --format=%H -- <source_dir>, ~2ms per extension) and compare in a command-gate-in.sh-level preflight, rather than relying on verify-deploy.sh (563 lines, 11 content-diffing gates, only invoked from skill-orchestrate's inter-cycle checkpoint -- not preflight-cheap and has the same deploy-required-to-fix-deploy bootstrap gap as any other deployed detector).
